examples.primaryText: John hopes which student will sing.
Mary worries that John didn't go to school yesterday.
Al's father worries where he can dock his boat.
examples.context: Al's father recently bought a new boat and is visiting Amsterdam with it. He is sure that there must be a place in Amsterdam where he can dock his boat, and he would be happy to dock his boat anywhere. However, for any specific place, he does not know whether it still has spots available, and he is anxiously trying to find out where exactly he can dock his boat.

examples.primaryText: Al's father worries that he can dock his boat at Y.
examples.context: Al's father recently bought a new boat and is visiting Amsterdam with it. He is sure that there must be a place in Amsterdam where he can dock his boat, and he would be happy to dock his boat anywhere. However, for any specific place, he does not know whether it still has spots available, and he is anxiously trying to find out where exactly he can dock his boat.
examples.comment: false for every choice of Y

examples.primaryText: Mr. Nelson denies he is “a real collector – the kind of person who buys first and then worries where he can find room for his purchases.”
As Ashley hands his church keys back he worries where he can spend the night.
I have a sister in California that worries where she can live because she is white and her kids are mixed race.
Lucas tells Sami that he loves her and Sami tells him that she loves him too. Sami worries what she can do since she loves them both.
Sam worries what they should wear.
examples.context: Sam is invited to an event. Not knowing much about it, they do not know what type of clothes would be appropriate: Casual, business casual, formal? They possess all relevant types of clothes and are happy to wear anything as long as it is appropriate for the occasion.

examples.primaryText: Sam worries that they should wear casual/business casual/formal.

examples.primaryText: John doesn't like which student will sing.
examples.context: It is common knowledge that John knows which student will sing. Al knows that there is no particular student John wants to sing (i.e., John is indifferent about which student will sing). Bo asks Al: “How does John feel about which student will sing?”

examples.primaryText: John isn't happy about which student will sing.

examples.primaryText: John doesn't hate which student will sing.
examples.context: It is common knowledge that John knows which student will sing. Al knows that there is no student such that John will hate it or be upset if they will sing. Bo asks Al: “How does John feel about which student will sing?”

examples.primaryText: Interstellar space is so vast that there is no need to fear whether stars in the Andromeda galaxy will accidentally slam into the Sun.
I fear whether this test would run safely on the oxygen sensor as it has a lot of drawback when compared with the others.
[...] I fear whether I'll have use of my arms/hands by age 55 or 60.
I know parents who seriously fear whether their children will ever hold a meaningful job.

Both women initially worried about taking the bus, fearing who else might be riding the bus. Both have been pleasantly surprised. Express bus seats recline, and have individual reading lights and air-conditioning vents.
But if my party doesn't enter this city, I fear who else will.
examples.comment: Martha Wells, The Edge of Worlds

examples.primaryText: The women do not fear who else might be riding the bus.
examples.context: There exists no person x such that the women fear that x might be riding the bus.
